raw_response:
I have been farming this land for 20 years, and with only 2.6 mu, every decision is about making sure my family of seven has enough to eat. Some of my family work off-farm and send money home, which helps us buy inputs, but I still watch every yuan because this land is small and there is no room for failure. I did not go far in school, so I do not read those extension leaflets, but I know what works from experience and from watching my neighbors, especially Old Wang whose field is next to mine.

For the winter wheat, I will plant my usual improved variety in early October — the same seed I bought from the township supply store last year because it sprouted well and the stalks were strong. I will hire the rotary tiller to prepare the ground, then spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as a base dressing. At green-up and again at jointing, I will topdress with urea. I know fertilizer is expensive now, but last year I got about 900 jin per mu and I want to keep it there, so I will put down about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu in total, plus some phosphorus and potassium. Water from the well costs electricity, but wheat cannot go thirsty, so I will irrigate three times: once after sowing to help it settle, once at jointing, and once when the heads are filling. I will spray twice — a herbicide in early spring and an insecticide only if I see aphids or rust.

For the summer maize, there is almost no time after the wheat harvest in mid-June, so I will quickly rotary till and plant hybrid maize seed the same day or the next. Everyone around here uses hybrid maize; the seed is more expensive but the yield is much better than traditional types, and with only 2.6 mu I need every kilogram. I will apply compound fertilizer at planting and then urea at the big trumpet stage, about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu total, plus a little phosphorus and potassium. Maize can handle dry weather better than wheat, and summer sometimes brings rain, so I will plan to irrigate twice — once at seedling stage if it is dry, and once at the trumpet stage. I will spray herbicide right after planting and insecticide later if the corn borers appear. If the weather is normal, I expect about 1,000 jin per mu from the maize.
